verdict: Occidental's sales jumped 53% to $8.1 billion and profit surged as oil prices rose sharply, generating $3.0 billion of free cash flow that helped cut debt by $1.9 billion.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Net sales $8.07B, up from $5.26B a year ago, on much higher oil prices

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Net income for common stockholders $2.81B; adjusted EPS from continuing operations was $2.40

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Free cash flow before working capital — the highest since Q3 2022

kpis.label: Production
kpis.note: Thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day — above the high end of guidance

segments.name: Oil & Gas
segments.note: Selling crude oil, natural gas liquids and gas, mostly from the Permian Basin and the Gulf of America — worldwide realized oil prices jumped to $96.78 a barrel.

segments.name: Midstream & Marketing
segments.note: Pipelines, processing and trading energy, shown net of $143M of eliminations (gross sales $1,326M) — a windfall quarter as crude and gas marketing margins spiked.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — headquarters, legal and support teams.

opex.name: Other operating & non-operating expense
opex.note: Other running costs outside the fields, as reported by Occidental.

otherDetail: Other income of $288M: $82M of interest and dividend income, $180M of gains on asset sales and $134M from equity investments (including its Western Midstream stake), less $108M of interest expense.
footerNote: Q3 2026 had not been reported as of November 7, 2026 — Occidental furnished only preliminary Q3 operating metrics on October 13 — so this page covers Q2 2026, the latest reported quarter. Adaptation for an oil producer: lease operating expense ($1,117M), transportation and gathering ($463M), depreciation, depletion and amortization ($1,847M), taxes other than income tax ($342M), exploration ($37M) and asset impairments ($38M) are grouped as the direct cost stage. Net income in the flow is income from continuing operations ($3,000M); after $19M for noncontrolling interests, $170M of preferred dividends and a $4M discontinued-operations loss, $2,807M was attributable to common stockholders.
oneTimers: Items Occidental calls out as affecting comparability added $368M after tax in Q2 — including $178M of midstream derivative gains, $199M of gains on asset sales and a $47M early debt-extinguishment gain. Adjusted income from continuing operations was $2,443M ($2.40 per share) versus $2,811M GAAP.
Debt fell fast: Occidental repaid $1.9B in the quarter, cutting principal debt to $11.8B on the way to its $10B milestone.

takeaways.title: Oil prices did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Worldwide realized oil prices rose 38% from Q1 to $96.78 a barrel — the single biggest reason sales jumped 53% and oil and gas pretax income reached $2.8B.

takeaways.title: A free-cash-flow machine this quarter
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $5.1B and free cash flow before working capital $3.0B — the best since 2022 — funding a $1.9B debt paydown and an 8% dividend increase to $0.28 a share.

takeaways.title: Production beat guidance
takeaways.text: Output averaged 1,433 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day, above the high end of guidance, led by the Permian and the Gulf of America.
